evidence: Built a pairwise observable map over all 49 graded criteria (2 gate, 37 functional, 5 polish, 5 visual). No two criteria grade the same primary observable and no pair demands incompatible products. The authors carved shared territory explicitly: hro_arrive_bottom 'Arrival of several cards together belongs to hro_bulk_move'; hro_interview_full 'Overfill by a multi-card move belongs to hro_bulk_places and by undo to hro_undo_full'; hro_undo_restores 'The A2 undo in B(12) is graded only in hro_undo_conflict'; hro_drafts 'Clearing the box after sending is graded in hro_msg_compose'; hro_candidate_view 'Whether other people's applications appear is graded only in hro_candidate_private; a candidate's reply is graded in hro_msg_exchange'; hro_candidate_linked 'This row alone owns that link'; hro_pol_live_thread 'This row owns the draft and focus; where the view goes while reading earlier messages is graded in Functional'; hro_pol_failed_send 'Unsaved note drafts are graded only in hro_pol_session_resume'; functional prompt.md line 19 'an Activity line added by a refused action is deducted only in hro_activity_refusals' and line 23 'Never deduct one observed defect in more than one row'. Role/refusal rows are partitioned by actor and verb with no overlap: hro_observer_readonly (Observer move/add/open-job/note writes), hro_candidate_no_staff (candidate writes), hro_candidate_private (candidate reads/leaks), hro_anonymous (401 for unauthenticated read/move/add/note/message), hro_thread_access (message send by Observer/Ingrid/Noor), hro_mgr_early_refused / hro_mgr_late_stages / hro_mgr_other_job / hro_notes (manager scope by stage, job and note). Server refusal vs UI recovery are distinct promises: hro_interview_full (server refuses, card stays; replay refused) vs hro_refused_put_back (page shows real place, reason, focus) - an app enforcing only client-side passes the latter and fails the former, so neither subsumes the other (REVIEW_POLICY: 'refusing a stale save and preserving the dirty editor are different outcomes'). Single vs multi-card validation (hro_move_one_stage/hro_interview_full vs hro_bulk_all_or_none/hro_bulk_places) are distinct public promises (hireops_rules.md:106-109 'Every card must satisfy all the rules above ... If any card fails, none of them moves'), and a separate bulk path that skips validation is a realistic defect the split catches. Functional arrival rows vs polish preservation rows (hro_live_board vs hro_pol_live_board; hro_msg_exchange vs hro_pol_live_thread) grade different promises from instruction.md:5 and :7 (update arrives vs nothing is disturbed); the polish rows' 'If no update arrives within 15 seconds ... this row is 0' is a required positive control (REVIEW_POLICY: 'A dead feature must not earn credit for doing nothing'), not a duplicate grade. Incompatibility check: success/failure send semantics (hro_msg_compose empty+focused after success vs hro_pol_failed_send text kept on failure), per-person drafts (hro_drafts persistence across reload vs hro_pol_session_resume hidden from Mei, kept for Rafael), candidate 404 vs anonymous 401 vs staff 403 semantics, and 'hiding is optional' clauses vs 'must be possible through ordinary non-drag controls' clauses all coexist in one conforming product consistent with hireops_rules.md sections 1, 3, 6. Probes tried: (a) broken app that could pass because one row stands in for another - none found; every refusal row carries its own same-kind control and the gate rows carry zero weight (scoring.toml gates 0.0). (b) conforming app that could fail from contradictory criteria - none found. Non-blocking P3 notes: (1) Positive controls re-observe a sibling's observable: 'own applications and conversations load' is graded in hro_candidate_view and is also the stated control of hro_candidate_no_staff and hro_candidate_private; an app whose candidate conversation fails to open while the list loads could be zeroed in all three under a strict reading, which sits in tension with prompt line 23 'Never deduct one observed defect in more than one row' (explicit zero rule only covers 'receives none of its own data'). Policy endorses reusing an observed fact as a control, so this is wording variance, not a duplicate criterion. (2) Visual hro_vis_type anchor 5 says 'deliberate hierarchy' while hro_vis_hierarchy grades prominence; overlap is mild, mirrors the template's own visual_typography/visual_hierarchy_and_scanability partition, and visual prompt.md says 'Do not deduct the same observed defect in more than one row'. (3) hro_bulk_move's first leg (board order Y, W, X) depends on hro_reorder's Y move-up having worked; the second leg (A2, V mixed-stage) still distinguishes board order from selection order, so the row remains decidable. This verdict is a source-level design review; no configured judge run measured how the judge resolves the control/no-double-deduction wording.
